status_summary: Both general counsels were removed within the first weeks of the term: law-firm reports date the removals of NLRB General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo and EEOC General Counsel Karla Gilbride to 2025-01-27, along with NLRB Board member Gwynne Wilcox and EEOC commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels, whose terms had not expired. At the NLRB, the agency's list of general counsels shows Abruzzo's tenure ending 2025-01-28, Jessica Rutter as acting general counsel from 2025-01-28 to 2025-02-01, and William Cowen as acting general counsel from 2025-02-01 (a law-firm report dates his designation 2025-02-03); Crystal Carey is now General Counsel, sworn in 2026-01-07. At the EEOC, Andrew Rogers was named acting general counsel on 2025-02-04; the EEOC's own list shows Rogers acting from January to October 2025 and Catherine Eschbach acting from October 2025 to September 2026 (month-only dates), with no successor named on that page. Carter Crow was nominated in November 2025; Bloomberg Government reported on 2026-04-28 that the White House withdrew the nomination, and no later nominee was found, so the EEOC has had no permanent general counsel. On 2026-06-29 the Supreme Court held in Trump v. Slaughter that the FTC commissioners' for-cause removal protection is unconstitutional; the opinion did not decide the status of the NLRB or EEOC, and a law-firm analysis dated 2026-07-02 says Wilcox had not filed a certiorari petition.

timeline.event: President Trump removes NLRB General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo and Board member Gwynne Wilcox, and EEOC General Counsel Karla Gilbride and Commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels. A law firm client alert reports that the removals left both agencies without a quorum and that the EEOC commissioners' terms ran to July 2028 and July 2026.

William Cowen becomes NLRB Acting General Counsel, replacing Jessica Rutter, who had been acting since 2025-01-28, per the NLRB's list of general counsels; a law-firm report dates the President's designation of Cowen 2025-02-03.
President Trump names Andrew Rogers, who had been chief counsel to then-Acting Chair Andrea Lucas, as EEOC Acting General Counsel.

Catherine Eschbach began serving as EEOC Acting General Counsel in October 2025 (month-only date), succeeding Andrew Rogers, who had been acting since January 2025, per the EEOC's list of its general counsels.

President Trump nominates M. Carter Crow, a Norton Rose Fulbright labor and employment partner, as EEOC General Counsel; a trade report dated 2025-11-19 says Catherine Eschbach was then acting general counsel and that Rogers had left to become Wage and Hour Division Administrator. No Senate action was found.
Crystal Carey is sworn in as NLRB General Counsel, per the NLRB's General Counsel page (the page gives the swearing-in date but not the confirmation date).
A law-firm article reports Catherine Eschbach, the principal deputy general counsel, is serving as EEOC Acting General Counsel and that the November 2025 nominee has not been confirmed.

Bloomberg Government reports that the White House sent the Senate a notice withdrawing the nomination of Carter Crow as EEOC general counsel (the notice was sent on the preceding Monday); the EEOC has had no permanent general counsel since January 2025.

In Trump v. Slaughter (decided 2026-06-29; Roberts, C.J., for the Court, 6-3) the Supreme Court holds that the FTC's for-cause removal protection violates the separation of powers and that the President may remove FTC commissioners, and overrules Humphrey's Executor to the extent anything remains of it. Part III-B (slip op. 27 to 28) reserves the Federal Reserve, non-Article III courts and bodies without executive power; the NLRB appears only in a citation (slip op. 23). The case is reversed and remanded.

A law-firm analysis reads Trump v. Slaughter as strongly signaling that NLRB members' removal protection is unconstitutional, notes the Court has not ruled on the NLRB, and says Wilcox had not filed a certiorari petition.
Catherine Eschbach's service as EEOC Acting General Counsel ended in September 2026 (month-only date), per the EEOC's list of its general counsels, which names no successor.
